status:
Extracted from the kernel monolith (Phase S, spec/PHASEMAP-v4.md) -- 33 real functions + 20 module-level state variables moved. Real, critical bug found and fixed during the extraction, not after: initRTC()'s peer.on('call', ...) handler and every other PeerJS event handler (including the very first 'peer ready' callLog() call) fire regardless of which tab is currently active -- initRTC() itself runs on login, not on visiting Call. Since call.js is lazily loaded (only fetched once the Call tab is actually mounted), an incoming call while on any other tab would have hit undefined functions. Fixed at the real root: initRTC() is now async and awaits eravosStampTab('call') (idempotent, a real no-op if already loaded) before registering any handler. Verified directly, not assumed: confirmed callLog/setupCallHandlers were genuinely undefined before a fresh account's first initRTC() call, and genuinely defined after -- with the person's currently-visible tab left completely undisturbed (call.html mounts silently in the background, doesn't force a navigation).

Previous status: mechanically extracted — hooks not yet scoped/typed in kernel. startCall() now sends a request first instead of ringing immediately — same shape as fabInviteToSpar()/spar:match_invite: emitSync('call:invite', ...), then the receiving side gets an actionable toast (showActionToast, now with an explicit Decline button, not just Accept+timeout) and 30s to accept or decline. No camera/mic is touched on either side until the invite is accepted; only then does the original requester actually peer.call() (see _ringPartner()), and the accepter auto-answers via a callId match in peer.on('call') rather than showing a second prompt. cancelCallRequest() lets the requester back out of a pending request. The old direct incoming-call banner (_pendingCall/showIncomingCall/answerCall/declineCall) is left in place as a fallback for any call that arrives without a matching accepted invite. Added screen sharing ('couch party'): toggleScreenShare() composites the screen + a small camera bubble onto a canvas and sends that single canvas.captureStream() track via RTCRtpSender.replaceTrack() on the existing PeerJS MediaConnection, so the partner needs no changes — they just receive one normal video track. Video-call only (no renegotiation path for audio-only calls yet). Added toggleCallFullscreen() on #call-video-grid via the Fullscreen API. Added Phase 4's 'Conversation Transcription' exactly as specced in the roadmap: toggleCallTranscription() runs the same local SpeechRecognition used by the Mythos voice-input toggle, one instance per device listening to that device's own mic only (no way to feed the remote WebRTC track into it, which is also what gives free speaker attribution — your device only ever transcribes you). Each finalized line is emitSync'd as 'call:transcript_line' so both sides end up with one merged transcript, and every line is pushed to eravors_call_transcripts, which buildLatticeData() now reads — so the conversation itself feeds the lattice (and, via saveToVault/sendToCodex downstream, the mythos) live, as a shared artifact rather than something one person builds alone. Unsupported on iOS Safari per the roadmap's own platform matrix; isVoiceToTextSupported() gates it the same way it gates the Mythos field.
